info.name: Buildiq — version diff (QUARANTINED, REQ-OBV-005)
info.description:
@newman exclude quarantined: asserts a REQ-OBV-005 grammar the controller does not implement, see tests/integration/quarantine/README.md. Rewriting it to match today's behaviour would turn a product gap into a fixed-looking test.

⚠️ QUARANTINED, NOT FIXED. Read tests/integration/quarantine/README.md.

This was the `REQ-OBV-005 — diff endpoint returns both manifest blobs` folder of buildiq-versioning.postman_collection.json, carrying the note 'STILL RED, DELIBERATELY'. It contributed three of the twelve Newman assertion failures on `development`. It is not run by CI (the Newman job globs tests/integration/*.postman_collection.json non-recursively), and it is preserved verbatim rather than rewritten.

Why it cannot simply be pointed at working values:

1. It diffs two SIBLING SNAPSHOT ROWS. ADR-002 retired those — publishing creates no sibling ApplicationVersion (openspec/specs/openbuild-version-snapshots/spec.md, REQ-OBV-002) — so `v2_uuid` is never assigned and the request leaves with an empty `to`. resolveVersionBlob() treats an empty token as a miss and the endpoint answers 404, which is correct behaviour.
2. The remaining gap is a genuine spec-vs-controller divergence. REQ-OBV-005 defines the refs as an ApplicationVersion SLUG, or `current:<versionSlug>`, or `history:<versionSlug>:<revisionId>`, returning `{ from: { manifest, semver, savedAt }, to: {…} }`. ApplicationsController::resolveVersionBlob() accepts only the literal `draft` or an ApplicationVersion UUID and returns `{ manifest, version, publishedAt }`.

Rewriting these three assertions against today's UUID behaviour would make them pass and would delete the only executable record that the endpoint and its specification disagree. It moves back to tests/integration/ when the ref grammar is implemented.

Running this by hand needs `v1_uuid`/`v2_uuid`, which the parent collection's setup folder assigned; supply them as env vars.
